newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 22.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 22. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Indonesian President Suharto has said the nation's unity must be upheld during the general election campaign which will start on Sunday. Indonesians will go to the polls on May 29.

President Suharto said the controversial national car programme would go ahead despite a Japanese government decision to bring the policy before a World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel. The national car programme launched in early 1996 grants tax and duty exemptions to PT Timor Putra, controlled by Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, to produce sedans bearing the Timor brandname.

A joint venture has been set up to build a $2.5 billion three level transit system linking south Jakarta and downtown Kota starting in December. The road-link will consist of a toll road, a railway track and a public road.

President Suharto will inaugurate a one million hectare rice field project in Central Kalimantan province on April 23. The government has built tens of kilometres of main and primary water channels within the confines of the mega project.
